statement: Constrained HBM supply is the stated driver of the Rubin Ultra downgrade: limiting memory per accelerator is described as a way to raise aggregate output under a fixed HBM pool.
why: It identifies HBM, not TSMC front-end wafer capacity, as the binding supply constraint for next-generation accelerators — the key question for how many GPUs can actually ship.

impact.mechanism: Tight HBM bit supply caps accelerator output, forcing spec reductions to stretch available memory across more units.

evidence.excerpt: limiting memory usage per accelerator enables higher aggregate output under constrained HBM supply
The framing is that relatively less-constrained TSMC front-end capacity is being balanced against tighter HBM supply.

confidence.basis: Secondary aggregation of one research note; no primary vendor or supplier filing.
